choices: The applicants who passed the written test last month.
The applicants who passed the test will be interviewed.
Although many applicants passed the written test last month.
After passing the written test, the applicants from our town.
answer: The applicants who passed the test will be interviewed.
hints: A long group of words can still be a fragment. Look for the main verb that goes with the main subject.
Words after "who" describe the subject. They are not its main verb. Cover the "who" part and see what is left.
For each choice, find the main subject, then look for its own verb. Cross out choices that start with "Although" or "After …" and never reach a main idea.

solution.methodName: Check for subject, verb and complete thought

steps.action: First choice: the main subject is "The applicants". "Who passed the written test last month" only describes them. There is no main verb, so it is a fragment.
steps.why: A "who" part tells which applicants. It does not say what they did or what will happen to them.

steps.action: Second choice: the main subject "The applicants" has its own verb, "will be interviewed". It is complete.
steps.why: Cover "who passed the test": "The applicants … will be interviewed." That is a full sentence.

steps.action: Third choice: "Although" makes the group of words depend on a main idea that never comes. It is a fragment.
Fourth choice: "After passing the written test" is an opening phrase. Then "the applicants from our town" has no verb. It is a fragment.
The complete sentence is "The applicants who passed the test will be interviewed."

trapNotes.The applicants who passed the written te: It has a verb, "passed", but that verb belongs to the "who" part. The main subject, "The applicants", never gets its own verb.
trapNotes.Although many applicants passed the writ: It has a subject and a verb, but "Although" signals that a main idea should follow, and it never does.
trapNotes.After passing the written test, the appl: It looks long and complete, but after the comma there is only a subject. What did the applicants do?
